full_judgment:
SM Ziaul Karim J: This Rule was issued, on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, at the instance of accused petitioner, calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceedings of GR Case No. 102 of 2005 (Sherpur) arising out of Sherpur Police Station Case No. 11 dated 29-9-2005 under sections 406, 420 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Bogra, should not be quashed. 

 3. The Police after investigation on 15-1-2006 submitted the charge sheet under sections 406, 420 of the Penal Code accusing four accused including the petitioner and the learned Magistrate, by the order dated 19-3-2006 accepted the same. The case is now pending in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Bogra. 

 4. On 7-9-2006 the accused petitioner filed an application before the learned Magistrate to decide the jurisdiction for the institution of the case. After hearing the learned Magistrate rejected the same. 

 6. Mr Saifur Reza, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, seeks to impeach the impugned proceedings on the two-fold arguments. Firstly, the allegations made in the first information report will come within the mischief of section 23 of the Emigration Ordinance (Ordinance No. XXIX of 1982). The Government by Notification has already constituted Special Court for the purpose of trial of all offences under the said Ordinance. Secondly, the ordinary Courts have no jurisdiction to try such offences, so the continuation of proceedings before the Court of Magistrate is the sheer abuse of the process of the Court and, as such, the same is liable to be quashed. In support of his contention he refers the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank Limited vs Tafazzal Hossain reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260 wherein it has been held: 

 9. Ongoing to the materials on record we find that the Police submitted charge sheet against four accused, of them only this petitioner being enlarged on bail preferred the instant application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and other accused are still absconding, of them, absconding accused, namely Md Mahbubur Rahinan (Swopan) and Md Tapash alias Makrjuk Rahman as petitioners, appeared before the High Court Division with an application for anticipatory bail but the same in rejected as not being pressed on 5-3-2006 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2966 of 2006. However, they were directed to surrender before the Court below at once. But without complying with the same they remained absconding. 

 10. Thereafter, one absconding accused, namely Md Tapash alias Mahrjuk Rahman as petitioner, filed Writ Petition No. 2313 of 2006 before the High Court Division challenging the proceedings of instant GR Case No. 102 of 2005 (Sherpur), pending before the Court of Magistrate, Bogra. In the said writ petition one of the Division Benches of the High Court Division by the order dated 19-3-2006 issued Rule and passed an order to the effect that the learned Magistrate is at liberty to proceed with the proceedings of GR Case No. 102 of 2005 (Sherpur) in accordance with law. Accordingly, the proceedings of the GR Case No. 102 of 2005 was continuing before the Court of learned Magistrate. The Rule is still pending for hearing, but suppressing such facts, the petitioner filed this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the same proceedings. We took it as exception. Suppression of such material facts is not desirable and, as such, the same is highly deprecated. 

 12. We find that in this particular case and individual lodged a first information report alleging that the accused took Taka 4,00,000 from him and another for the purpose of sending them abroad on employment but instead of sending them, they misappropriated the entire money and on repeated requests their money was not refunded rather, the accused denied to refund they money. The allegation prima facie attracts the mischief of the Penal Code. The Special Court under the Emigration Ordinance, 1982 is not authorised to try any offence either under section 406 or under section 420 of the Penal Code, far less exclusively. The informant has the option to activate prosecution of the accused under The Emigration Ordinance, 1982 as well, but if the allegations contain the ingredients of an offence or offences under the Penal Code, which are not far less exclusively triable, by a special Court, the informant's case before the Magistrate cannot be stifled by quashing. To that effect reliance is being placed in the case of Noor Jahan Begum vs State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner reported in 49 DLR (AD) 106 = 2 MLR (AD) 34 wherein it has been held: 

 "The complainant has the option to activate prosecution of the petitioners under The Emigration Ordinance, 1982 as well, but if the allegations contain the ingredients under the Penal Code, the complainant's case before the Magistrate cannot be stifled by quashing." 

 We have gone through the decision reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260 as referred by the learned Counsel for the petitioner, we are in respectful agreement with the principles enunciated therein but the facts leading to that case are quite distinguishable to that of the instant case. Therefore, the grounds urged and contentions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner, stand rejected as having been devoid of any substance. On the contrary, the legal plea taken by the learned Assistant Attorney-General prevails and appears to have a good deal of force. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. The proceedings of the GR Case No. 102 of 2005 (Sherpur) arising out of Sherpur Police Stating Case No. 11 dated 29-9-2005 under sections 406, 420 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Bogra, now Judicial Magistrate, Bogra, will proceed in accordance with law.
